title: Typography and Text Styling
subtitle: Make every word clear, readable, and well presented
description: Learn how to style fonts, control text size and spacing, align content, and create readable responsive typography.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Typography and Text Styling: concepts and applied practice

blocks.title: PAGE 1: Understanding Typography
blocks.text:
Typography is the way text is displayed on a page. It includes the font, size, weight, spacing, alignment, and line height. Good typography helps visitors read comfortably and understand which information is most important.

CSS uses font-family to choose a font. Provide fallback fonts in case the first font is unavailable. For example, font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif asks the browser to use Arial first, then Helvetica, then another available sans-serif font.

The font-size property controls text size. You may use pixels (px), em, or rem. The font-weight property controls how light or bold text appears. Common values include normal, bold, 400, and 700.

Do not choose text styles only because they look dramatic. Body text needs to be comfortable to read, and headings should make the page's structure clear. Keep a consistent style across similar elements.

blocks.output: The heading is larger and bold. The introductory paragraph is slightly larger than the normal paragraph.

blocks.title: How Sample Code 1 Works
blocks.text:
The body rule establishes the default font family, size, and text color. Descendants generally inherit properties such as font-family and color unless another rule overrides them.

The heading uses 2rem for its font size. If the root font size is 16px, 2rem equals 32px. The intro paragraph uses 1.125rem, which equals 18px with that same root size. The heading's font-weight of 700 requests a bold weight, while 400 is the usual normal weight.

A key professional habit is to distinguish each property's job. font-size changes size; font-weight changes the heaviness of the letters; font-family changes the typeface.

blocks.question: A heading looks too thin, but its size and typeface are already correct. Which property should you adjust first?
blocks.explanation: font-weight controls how light or bold text appears. The other properties control the typeface, alignment, or vertical spacing.
blocks.hint: Choose the property that controls the boldness of letters.

blocks.title: PAGE 2: Line Height and Letter Spacing
blocks.text:
Text needs space as well as an appropriate font size. The line-height property controls the height of each line box and therefore the vertical space between lines. A value such as line-height: 1.6 gives the line box a height of roughly 1.6 times the element's font size. Unitless line-height values are often useful because they scale with text size.

The letter-spacing property adds or reduces space between characters. The word-spacing property controls spacing between words. These properties can help with small design adjustments, but too much letter spacing can make normal paragraphs difficult to read.

Long paragraphs are often easier to read with comfortable line height and controlled line length. If lines are too tightly packed, readers may lose their place. If lines are extremely far apart, the paragraph may feel disconnected. Test actual text instead of judging typography from a short heading alone.

blocks.title: Sample Code 2: Improving Paragraph Readability
blocks.code:

Use spacing carefully. The goal is clarity, not decoration for its own sake.
blocks.output: The text uses comfortable line height, a maximum article width, and subtle character and word spacing.

blocks.text: PAGE 2 — Typography and Text Styling: concepts and applied practice

blocks.title: Choose Spacing for the Reader
blocks.text:
The body rule sets line-height: 1.6, giving lines more vertical room than a tight line height such as 1.1. Because the value has no unit, it scales with the font size. The article's max-width limits how wide the text can grow on a large screen while allowing it to fit narrower available space.

The letter-spacing and word-spacing values are intentionally small. Large values can make sentences look broken apart, so do not increase them without a reason. Typography should support the message and the reader.

blocks.question: A long paragraph feels cramped because its lines are too close together. Which change most directly improves the vertical space between lines?
blocks.explanation: line-height controls the height of line boxes and is a direct way to improve vertical spacing between lines.
blocks.hint: Look for the property that controls the height of text lines.

blocks.title: PAGE 3: Alignment, Decoration, and Transformation
blocks.text:
CSS provides several properties for presenting text. text-align controls horizontal alignment inside a block. Common values include left, right, center, and justify. Left alignment is often a good default for paragraphs in left-to-right languages. Center alignment can work well for short headings, but long centered paragraphs can be harder to follow.

The text-decoration property can add or remove decorations such as underlines and line-through effects. Links are often underlined because the underline helps users recognize interactive text. Removing underlines from links should not make them difficult to identify.

The text-transform property changes displayed capitalization. uppercase displays letters in uppercase, lowercase displays them in lowercase, and capitalize changes the first letter of each word to uppercase. This changes how text is rendered; it does not rewrite the original text stored in HTML.

Use these properties with purpose. Alignment establishes a clear layout, decoration can communicate link behavior, and transformation can make labels consistent. Do not make interactive text look like ordinary text without providing another clear visual cue.

blocks.title: Understanding the Text Styles
blocks.text:
The h1 rule centers the heading and applies text-transform: capitalize. The description paragraph is left-aligned. The anchor rule gives links a blue color and an underline so they remain recognizable as links. The completed class adds a line through the task text.

Notice that text-transform affects displayed appearance rather than changing the original HTML text. An underline is not merely decoration in every context: for links, it can help users identify clickable text. Avoid removing visual cues unless you replace them with another clear cue.

blocks.question: A developer removes underlines from every link and leaves the links the same color as surrounding paragraph text. What is the main usability concern?
options: The browser will stop reading HTML
Visitors may struggle to recognize which text is clickable
The font size automatically becomes zero
The page can no longer use margins
blocks.explanation: Links need a clear visual distinction. If color and underline cues are removed without replacement, users may not recognize clickable text.
blocks.hint: Think about how a visitor knows which words are links.

blocks.title: PAGE 4: Responsive Typography and Text Hierarchy
blocks.text:
A professional page must remain readable on different screen sizes. A heading that looks good on a laptop may be too large for a phone, while a paragraph with very long lines may be tiring to read on a wide display. Responsive typography adjusts text presentation to the available space.

Media queries let you apply styles only when a condition is met. For example, you can reduce a large heading's font size on screens 600px wide or smaller. Another option is clamp(), which sets a preferred value with a minimum and maximum. For example, font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 5vw, 3rem) lets a heading scale with viewport width while keeping it within a chosen range.

Text hierarchy is the visual order that helps readers scan a page. Main headings should stand out from subheadings, and body text should remain comfortable to read. Use consistent sizes and weights for similar elements. Do not rely on color or size alone to communicate essential meaning; the actual HTML heading structure should also make sense.

blocks.title: Sample Code 4: Responsive Typography
blocks.code:
Typography That Adapts

Designed for Every Screen

Readable text helps learners focus on the lesson rather than struggle with the layout.
blocks.output: The main heading scales within limits, the article stays at a readable maximum width, and the smaller heading reduces in size on narrow screens.

blocks.title: Responsive Design Decisions
blocks.text:
The clamp() function takes a minimum, a preferred value, and a maximum. Here, the heading cannot become smaller than 1.8rem or larger than 3rem, while 5vw provides a viewport-based preferred size. This allows it to scale without growing or shrinking without limits.

The media query applies only when the viewport is 600px wide or narrower. It reduces body padding and the h2 font size for smaller screens. The max-width on the content container prevents lines from becoming excessively long on wide screens.

When testing typography, check small and large screens, zoom in, and read a real paragraph. Look for text that is clipped, crowded, too faint, or difficult to scan. Good typography combines CSS styling with meaningful HTML structure and sufficient contrast.

blocks.question: You want a heading to grow on wider screens but never become smaller than 1.8rem or larger than 3rem. Which option is designed for this purpose?
blocks.explanation: clamp() accepts a minimum, preferred, and maximum value. It allows a font size to scale within defined limits.
blocks.hint: Choose the function that sets a minimum and maximum size around a preferred value.

blocks.title: Final Challenge: Design a Readable Course Article
blocks.text:
Create a course article with one main heading, two subheadings, and several paragraphs. Choose a reliable font stack, set a comfortable body font size and line height, and make the main heading stand out using size and weight. Keep paragraphs within a sensible maximum width, style links so they are easy to recognize, and use responsive sizing for the main heading.

Test the page on your phone. Ask yourself: can I scan the headings quickly? Can I read the paragraphs without struggling? Are links easy to recognize? Does the heading fit without causing unwanted horizontal scrolling?

A strong design is not simply a collection of visual effects. It uses typography to make information understandable, accessible, and consistent.

blocks.question: A paragraph is difficult to read on a wide desktop because each line contains too many words. Which adjustment is most directly useful?
options: Give the paragraph a sensible max-width
Add a thick border around every word
blocks.explanation: A sensible max-width controls the line length and can make long paragraphs easier to follow on wide screens.
blocks.hint: Think about controlling how wide the text block can become.

blocks.question: Which statement correctly describes text-transform: uppercase?
options: It permanently rewrites the text in the HTML source
It changes the displayed capitalization through CSS
It increases the thickness of every letter
It adds a line through the text
blocks.explanation: text-transform changes how text is displayed. It does not rewrite the original text stored in HTML.
blocks.hint: Separate the original content from its visual presentation.

blocks.question: A page uses the same font size for its main heading, subheadings, and body text. What is the strongest design improvement?
options: Create a consistent type hierarchy using suitable sizes and weights
Use a different font family for every sentence
blocks.explanation: A consistent type hierarchy helps readers identify the main topic, supporting sections, and body content at a glance.
blocks.hint: Think about how visual differences can show the importance of information.

blocks.question: A heading looks excellent on a laptop but overflows on a phone. What is the best approach?
options: Add spaces manually inside the heading
Use responsive sizing or a suitable media query, then test at small widths
blocks.explanation: Responsive font sizing and media queries let text adapt to different viewport sizes. Testing helps confirm that the heading fits the available space.
blocks.hint: Choose a solution that adapts to the screen rather than forcing one fixed size.
